report.headline: You can challenge ₹11,600 of the ₹19,840 deducted
report.summary: 4 of 14 deductions don't hold up against your policy wording and IRDAI rules. If the insurer accepts, you could get about ₹11,020 more after the 5% co-pay. ₹3,600 (5 items) is part of room or procedure charges. The deduction is correct, but you can ask the hospital to waive it.

deduction_findings.insurer_reason: Diagnostic expenses not related to current treatment (Code Excl04)
deduction_findings.explanation: This exclusion only covers tests that are not related or incidental to the treatment. Examining the tissue removed during the laparoscopic cholecystectomy is part of that treatment.
"Examination Gloves (pairs)" is listed as "Gloves", which is in List I of your policy's Annexure-A (not covered). This deduction is correct.
"IV Cannula - Vasofix Safety 20G" is listed as "Vasofix safety", which is in List I of your policy's Annexure-A (not covered). This deduction is correct.
"Nebulizer Kit" is listed as "Nebulizer kit", which is in List I of your policy's Annexure-A (not covered). This deduction is correct.

deduction_findings.insurer_reason: Subsumed into procedure charges - List III
deduction_findings.explanation: "Gauze & Cotton (sterile)" is listed as "Cotton" and "Gauze", which is in List III of your policy's Annexure-A: it counts as part of the procedure charges, so it isn't paid as a separate line. Because this was cashless at a network hospital, you can ask the hospital to absorb it. That's a request, not a legal right.

deduction_findings.insurer_reason: Subsumed into room charges - List II

Because this was cashless at a network hospital, you can ask the hospital to absorb it. That's a request, not a legal right.

deduction_findings.insurer_reason: Subsumed into cost of treatment - List IV
deduction_findings.explanation: "Registration Charges" is listed as "Admission/registration charges", which is in List IV of your policy's Annexure-A: it counts as part of the cost of treatment, so it isn't paid as a separate line. check_findings.explanation: 3 deductions only say things like "Non-payable consumables". When a claim is partly disallowed, the insurer must refer to the specific terms of the policy. Ask it to name the clause for each.
The 5% co-pay (₹5,993) was correctly applied to the admissible amount after deductions (₹1,19,860).

check_findings.issue: Specific waiting period: Calculi in urinary system, Gall Bladder and Bile duct, excluding malignancy
check_findings.explanation: Calculi in urinary system, Gall Bladder and Bile duct, excluding malignancy has a 24-month waiting period. Continuous cover since 10 Jan 2023 is 42 months at admission, so the waiting period is complete.

similar_cases.insurer_reason: Anaesthesia machine and gases are consumables forming part of OT charges under the standard definition of OT and should not be billed separately; OT and anaesthesia charges in the bill had already been paid. (Separately, Rs 17,947 of items such as caps, gauze, masks, gloves and food were deducted as non-payable.)
similar_cases.reasoning: The Forum noted that the hospital had billed the anaesthesia equipment and gases separately and clarified they were not part of OT charges; had they been included in OT charges the insurer would have paid them. Disallowing them merely because of how the hospital structured its bill was not justified, so the further Rs 10,890 was ordered to be paid.

similar_cases.insurer_reason: Rs 2,700 of nursing/RMO charges are included in room charges; Rs 23,837 was deducted as non-medical expenses, including Rs 7,392 for the drainage kit, which is not payable under clause 4.4.17 and Annexure II (item 180 - 'any kit not specified').
similar_cases.reasoning: The Forum held that the drainage kit is a non-medical item listed as not payable in Annexure II (item 180) of the policy, so the settlement was in order and no relief could be granted.

similar_cases.forum: State Commission Delhi (Delhi State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission)
similar_cases.insurer_reason: Deductions under exclusion 4.16 (external/durable medical equipment usable at home, e.g., knee support), 4.17 (non-medical items) and 4.26 (doctor's home visits and nursing/physiotherapy at home during pre- and post-hospitalisation), totalling Rs 78,490.
similar_cases.reasoning: Applying the principle that insurance contracts are construed strictly (Sushilaben Indravadan Gandhi v. New India Assurance, SC 2020), the State Commission held the deducted items fell within the exclusion clauses. It set aside the District Forum's order and directed payment of only the originally approved Rs 9,527 (with 9% interest if not paid by 31.03.2021).

escalation.title: Write to the insurer's grievance officer
escalation.action: Send the complaint letter ClaimBack drafts, listing each disputed amount and the clause or rule behind it. Keep proof of sending.
escalation.deadline_note: The insurer must acknowledge immediately and resolve it within 14 days, by 01 Oct 2026.

escalation.title: Register it on Bima Bharosa
escalation.action: Also log the complaint on IRDAI's Bima Bharosa portal (bimabharosa.irdai.gov.in) so it's tracked.
escalation.deadline_note: Optional, but it puts the complaint on IRDAI's record.

escalation.title: Go to the Insurance Ombudsman, Bengaluru
escalation.action: If the insurer rejects your complaint, doesn't reply, or replies unsatisfactorily, file with the Ombudsman online at cioins.co.in. It's free.
escalation.deadline_note: Possible after 30 days without a satisfactory reply. File within 1 year of the insurer's reply. Claims up to Rs 50 lakh.

escalation.title: Consumer commission (last resort)
escalation.action: If the Ombudsman route doesn't work for you, a district consumer commission can hear the dispute. You can't pursue both for the same dispute.
escalation.deadline_note: General information only; consider advice before filing.

R-OMBUDSMAN-ONE-YEAR-LIMIT.title: The Ombudsman complaint must be filed within one year of the insurer's rejection of the representation, of receiving its unsatisfactory decision, or of expiry of one month from sending the representation if no reply was received.
R-OMBUDSMAN-ONE-YEAR-LIMIT.quote: (b) The complaint is made within one year-- (i) after the order of the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be,] rejecting the representation is received; or (ii) after receipt of decision of the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be], which is not to the satisfaction of the complainant; (iii) after expiry of a period of one month from the date of sending the written representation to the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be,] if the insurer or 1 [ insurance broker, as the case may be], named fails to furnish reply to the complainant.

R-OMBUDSMAN-PRECONDITION-APPROACH-INSURE.title: Before going to the Ombudsman, the complainant must have made a written/email/online representation to the insurer, and either it was rejected, no reply came within one month of the insurer receiving it, or the reply is unsatisfactory.
R-OMBUDSMAN-PRECONDITION-APPROACH-INSURE.quote: No complaint to the Insurance Ombudsman shall lie unless (a) the complainant 1 [has made a representation in writing or through electronic mail or online through website of the insurer or insurance broker concerned] named in the complaint and-- (i) either the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be,] had rejected the complaint; or (ii) the complainant had not received any reply within a period of one month after the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be,] received his representation; or (iii) the complainant is not satisfied with the reply given to him by the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be.]
R-OMBUDSMAN-PRECONDITION-APPROACH-INSURE.source_detail: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended up to 09.11.2023; CIO consolidated copy)

R-SPECIFIC-WAITING-MAX-36M.title: A specific-disease/treatment waiting period can be at most 36 months from policy commencement, does not apply to treatment needed due to an accident, and the disease/treatment must be covered once the period is completed with continuous renewal.
R-SPECIFIC-WAITING-MAX-36M.quote: "Specific waiting period" means a period up to 36 months from the commencement of a health insurance policy during which period specified diseases/treatments (except due to an accident) are not covered. On completion of the period, diseases/treatments shall be covered provided the policy has been continuously renewed without any break.

grievance.subject: Grievance: claim no. CLM-NHI-26-0845521, policy no. NHI/AS/2026/0073311
grievance.body:
Date: 17 September 2026

To
The Grievance Redressal Officer
Nirmaan Health Insurance Co. Ltd.

Subject: Grievance against deductions in claim no. CLM-NHI-26-0845521, policy no. NHI/AS/2026/0073311

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing about the above claim for the hospitalisation of Sunita Sharma at Lakeview Multispeciality Hospital from 03 August 2026 to 06 August 2026 (Symptomatic cholelithiasis (gallbladder stones) with chronic cholecystitis). Your office settled the claim by letter dated 06 August 2026, paying ₹1,13,867 against ₹1,39,700 claimed.

I have checked the decision against the policy wording (Arogya Sanjeevani Policy, Niva Bupa Health Insurance Co. Ltd. (UIN NBHHLIP27056V042627)) and IRDAI's regulations, and I dispute the following:

1. Sutures - Vicryl 2-0 / Prolene 3-0: ₹3,600 of the ₹3,600 deducted as "Non-payable consumables". This item isn't in the policy's lists of non-payable items (Annexure-A, List I-IV) and it is a medically necessary part of the surgery. An insurer can only deduct for exclusions actually written in the policy, and your letter cites no clause. (Ref: Policy wording: Section 4.7; IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024: Section 2, Chapter IV, para 16.3, Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(5))
2. Hem-o-lok Ligation Clips (Medium-Large): ₹4,200 of the ₹4,200 deducted as "Non-payable consumables". This item isn't in the policy's lists of non-payable items (Annexure-A, List I-IV) and it is a medically necessary part of the surgery. An insurer can only deduct for exclusions actually written in the policy, and your letter cites no clause. (Ref: Policy wording: Section 4.7; IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024: Section 2, Chapter IV, para 16.3, Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(5))
3. Closed Suction Drain Set (Romovac 14Fr): ₹1,450 of the ₹1,450 deducted as "Non-payable consumables". This item isn't in the policy's lists of non-payable items (Annexure-A, List I-IV). An insurer can only deduct for exclusions actually written in the policy, and your letter cites no clause. (Ref: Policy wording: Section 4.7; IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024: Section 2, Chapter IV, para 16.3, Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(5))
4. Histopathology - Gallbladder Specimen: ₹2,350 of the ₹2,350 deducted as "Diagnostic expenses not related to current treatment (Code Excl04)". This exclusion only covers tests that are not related or incidental to the treatment. Examining the tissue removed during the laparoscopic cholecystectomy is part of that treatment. (Ref: Policy wording: Section 7.1 (Code Excl04); IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024: Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(5))
5. Deduction letter does not cite policy clauses: 3 deductions only say things like "Non-payable consumables". When a claim is partly disallowed, the insurer must refer to the specific terms of the policy. (Ref: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024: Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(5))

I request you to pay the wrongly deducted ₹11,600 (about ₹11,020 after co-payment), and to reply with reasons that refer to the specific terms of the policy. I understand IRDAI requires grievances to be acknowledged immediately and resolved within 14 days. Subject: Complaint against Nirmaan Health Insurance Co. Ltd. - claim no. CLM-NHI-26-0845521, policy no. NHI/AS/2026/0073311

Respected Sir/Madam,

1. Complainant: Sunita Sharma, policyholder under policy no. NHI/AS/2026/0073311 (Arogya Sanjeevani Policy) issued by Nirmaan Health Insurance Co. Ltd.

2. The claim: hospitalisation of Sunita Sharma at Lakeview Multispeciality Hospital, Bengaluru, from 03 August 2026 to 06 August 2026 for Symptomatic cholelithiasis (gallbladder stones) with chronic cholecystitis. Amount claimed: ₹1,39,700. Amount paid: ₹1,13,867.

3. The insurer's decision: partial settlement by letter dated 06 August 2026.

4. I first represented to the insurer in writing on [date of your grievance] and [the insurer rejected it on (date) / did not reply within one month / replied on (date) and I am not satisfied]. (Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended up to 09.11.2023; CIO consolidated copy), Rule 14(3)(a) (as amended by G.S.R. 147(E) dated 02.03.2021))

5. Grounds of complaint:

1. Sutures - Vicryl 2-0 / Prolene 3-0: ₹3,600 of the ₹3,600 deducted as "Non-payable consumables". This item isn't in the policy's lists of non-payable items (Annexure-A, List I-IV) and it is a medically necessary part of the surgery. An insurer can only deduct for exclusions actually written in the policy, and your letter cites no clause. (Ref: Policy wording: Section 4.7; IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024: Section 2, Chapter IV, para 16.3, Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(5))
2. Hem-o-lok Ligation Clips (Medium-Large): ₹4,200 of the ₹4,200 deducted as "Non-payable consumables". This item isn't in the policy's lists of non-payable items (Annexure-A, List I-IV) and it is a medically necessary part of the surgery. An insurer can only deduct for exclusions actually written in the policy, and your letter cites no clause. (Ref: Policy wording: Section 4.7; IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024: Section 2, Chapter IV, para 16.3, Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(5))
3. Closed Suction Drain Set (Romovac 14Fr): ₹1,450 of the ₹1,450 deducted as "Non-payable consumables". This item isn't in the policy's lists of non-payable items (Annexure-A, List I-IV). An insurer can only deduct for exclusions actually written in the policy, and your letter cites no clause. (Ref: Policy wording: Section 4.7; IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024: Section 2, Chapter IV, para 16.3, Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(5))
4. Histopathology - Gallbladder Specimen: ₹2,350 of the ₹2,350 deducted as "Diagnostic expenses not related to current treatment (Code Excl04)". This exclusion only covers tests that are not related or incidental to the treatment. Examining the tissue removed during the laparoscopic cholecystectomy is part of that treatment. (Ref: Policy wording: Section 7.1 (Code Excl04); IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024: Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(5))
5. Deduction letter does not cite policy clauses: 3 deductions only say things like "Non-payable consumables". When a claim is partly disallowed, the insurer must refer to the specific terms of the policy. (Ref: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024: Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(5))

Relief sought: direct the insurer to pay ₹11,020 (the wrongly deducted amount after co-payment) with interest at bank rate + 2% from the date the claim was reported.

I confirm that the same dispute is not pending before, and has not been decided by, any court, consumer forum or arbitrator.

Enclosures: policy schedule and wording, hospital bill, discharge summary, insurer's letter dated 06 August 2026, my grievance and the insurer's reply (if any).

Yours faithfully,
Sunita Sharma
